candidates.title: Certified Lipschitz Robustness Audits of Convolutional EEG Decoders Across Standardized BCI Benchmarks
candidates.summary: This proposal asks how robust standard EEG decoders actually are, using guarantees rather than attacks alone. SDP-based Lipschitz upper bounds would be computed for EEGNet, ShallowConvNet and DeepConvNet trained on several open motor-imagery and ERP datasets. The bounds would be turned into certified input-perturbation radii for each trial. These radii would be compared with sampled CLEVER estimates and with the smallest perturbations found by PGD and universal-perturbation attacks. All radii would be expressed in microvolts relative to typical EEG noise and artifact amplitudes. The aim is to test whether certified safety margins for BCI decoders are smaller than ordinary physiological noise, and how this differs by architecture and dataset.
candidates.gap: The cited work shows that EEG CNNs can be fooled by adversarial and universal perturbations, and it studies how to detect such attacks. However, none of it gives formal, attack-independent robustness guarantees for EEG decoders. The SDP Lipschitz methods and CLEVER were tested on image or toy classifiers, not on EEG networks with depthwise spatial filters. No cited work compares certified margins with how large EEG signals and noise really are.
candidates.approach: Convert the convolutional, depthwise-spatial and separable layers of EEGNet and ShallowConvNet into equivalent linear operators, and treat the ELU and square/log nonlinearities as slope-restricted for the quadratic-constraint SDP. For large layers, use the layer-wise decomposition to keep the SDP tractable. From the logit margin and the Lipschitz bound, derive per-trial certified L2 radii. Run this across MOABB datasets with within-subject and cross-subject splits.
candidates.evaluation: Certified radii from the SDP bounds would be compared with naive bounds from products of layer norms, with CLEVER estimates, and with empirical minimal perturbations from PGD and from the total-loss-minimization universal perturbation attack. Measures: tightness ratio of certified to empirical radius; certified accuracy at microvolt-scale radii; and how radius relates to signal-to-noise ratio across paradigms and datasets. MOABB's multi-dataset protocol would be used for reproducibility.

candidates.title: Parseval-Constrained EEGNet: Lipschitz-Bounded BCI Decoders with Certifiable Robustness to Universal Perturbations
candidates.summary: This proposal tests whether the Lipschitz constant can be built into compact EEG decoders without losing decoding accuracy. EEGNet's temporal, depthwise-spatial and separable convolutions would be constrained during training to be approximately Parseval tight frames. The resulting models would be compared with unconstrained EEGNet, PGD adversarially trained EEGNet, and Cross-Lipschitz-regularized EEGNet. Comparisons would cover clean accuracy, empirical robustness to PGD and universal adversarial perturbations, and SDP-certified Lipschitz bounds, all across several MOABB datasets. The hypothesis is that Lipschitz control fits the spatial-filtering structure of EEG well and gives a better trade-off between accuracy and certified robustness than adversarial training.
candidates.gap: Parseval networks and Cross-Lipschitz regularization were developed and tested on image benchmarks. The EEG adversarial work focuses on attacks and detection, not on training decoders that are robust by construction. It is also unknown whether orthogonality constraints on EEGNet's spatial filters hurt its small-data performance across paradigms.
candidates.approach: During SGD, add Parseval retraction steps for EEGNet's temporal, depthwise-spatial, pointwise and dense layers, and use convex aggregation for any residual or pooling paths. Variants would constrain only the spatial filters versus all layers. Train both within-subject and cross-subject, and compute certified Lipschitz bounds after training with the SDP method.
candidates.evaluation: Baselines: vanilla EEGNet and ShallowConvNet, FBCSP, PGD adversarial training, and Cross-Lipschitz regularization. Measures: clean accuracy or AUC on MOABB motor-imagery and P300 datasets; accuracy under PGD and under total-loss-minimization universal perturbations; SDP Lipschitz upper bound and certified accuracy at fixed microvolt radii; and training cost.

candidates.title: Lipschitz-Margin Certificates as Runtime Safety Monitors for BCI-Controlled Effectors
candidates.summary: This proposal turns per-instance robustness certificates into a runtime monitor that stops a BCI from issuing a command when it cannot be certified. For each EEG trial, a certified radius is computed from the logit margin and a precomputed SDP Lipschitz bound, or from the instance-specific Cross-Lipschitz bound. When the radius falls below a threshold set to the noise level, the system abstains instead of driving an assistive device. The monitor would be compared with Mahalanobis- and cosine-distance adversarial detectors. Tests would cover white-box attacks, universal perturbations, unseen attacks, and natural artifacts. The aim is to test whether certificates generalize to unknown threats better than learned detectors.
candidates.gap: Existing EEG adversarial detectors are statistical and learned. They perform well on white-box attacks they were tuned for, but transfer less reliably to unknown attacks, and they give no guarantee. The safety and neurosecurity literature calls for monitoring and safe failure in BCIs that control physical effectors, but no cited work links formal robustness certificates to abstention decisions in BCIs.
candidates.approach: Precompute global or layer-wise SDP Lipschitz bounds for the trained decoder. At inference, compute the instance-specific certified radius, which can also be combined with local gradient-norm estimates, and abstain when it is below a threshold tau. Tau is calibrated on clean validation data to meet a target false-abstention rate. A simulated closed-loop cursor or effector task would measure how often unsafe commands get through.
candidates.evaluation: Baselines: Mahalanobis and cosine-distance detectors, softmax-confidence thresholding, and no monitor. Measures: detection AUC against PGD, FGSM, universal and natural-artifact perturbations, including transfer to attacks not seen during calibration; risk-coverage curves; rate of unsafe commands let through in simulated control; and computational latency. Evaluation would span several MOABB datasets and EEGNet and ShallowConvNet.
